name: vehicle-fast-transport
description: Issue #1093 (mount/itinerary rebuild phase 7): a distant on-foot general_work order (requiredVehicleRole: null) is dispatched to a driller who also holds the driving.truck licence, with one free tier-1 debris hauler ($25,000, speed 3) parked near the driller's own spawn point. VEHICLE_TRANSPORT_PLANNING_ENABLED's planner comparison, wired through planItinerary (findCheapestTransportItinerary), has the driller board the hauler, ride most of the ~15-cell trip at speed 3 rather than walking the whole way at AGENT_WALK_SPEED (2), alight within TRANSPORT_ALIGHT_FINISH_WALK_CELLS of the target, and finish on foot -- driverBoardingCount (vehicleBoardingCount in the state dump) reads at least 1 by the time the order resolves, and the hauler releases cleanly (no reservation, no occupant) once it does.

steps.description: Spawns near world centre (~16,16) -- close to both the debris hauler bought below and far from the dispatched target on the map's east edge.

Grants the licence a debris hauler's driver seat requires (ROLE_LICENCE_REQUIRED.debris_hauler, gameplay-vehicle-fleet). No UI control hands out an exact licence for free -- the player-facing path is Driving Center training -- so this is a bootstrap primitive, same class as every other assign_skill step in the suite.

Spawns near world centre too (purchaseVehicle's own grid-centre stagger, vehicle.ts) -- close enough to the driller for boarding to be cheap, and fast enough (speed 3, vs AGENT_WALK_SPEED 2) that riding most of the way to the far dispatch target below should beat walking it outright.

A far, plain on-foot order -- requiredVehicleRole: null, ~15 cells from the driller's own spawn point -- exactly the goal shape phase 7's planner comparison targets (gameplay-vehicle-fleet: 'For an on-foot action the planner may compare walking against [foot -> vehicle, board, drive, alight, foot -> target] and pick the cheaper'). No UI control drives this exact dispatch (employees.ts's own case comment), same bootstrap primitive nav-pathfinding-visual.json already uses.

Advances time until the dispatched order resolves (pendingActionCount drops back to 0, TaskLifecycleCore.ts's own splice-on-completion), rather than a hand-measured tick pad -- see dev-scenario-authoring's wait-on-a-condition rule. With findCheapestTransportItinerary wired into planItinerary, the driller rides the hauler for most of the trip and vehicleBoardingCount moves off its starting 0 by the time this step's own goal is checked.

expect.note: vehicleBoardingCount (state.vehicles.driverBoardingCount) rising by at least 1 during this wait is the proof the driller actually boarded the free hauler rather than walking the whole ~15-cell trip -- the same field tutorial-boxcut-full.json's own atMost ceiling already uses for this purpose. atMost:2 bounds it: one board leg to reach the hauler, at most one more if an interruption ever forces a re-board, never the walk-the-whole-way zero this order takes today.

steps.description: Once phase 7 lands, the hauler's own row should show it idle again -- no reservation, no driver -- released cleanly after the ride, mirroring vehicles.integration.test.ts's own post-arrival assertions for this same feature.
